title: CCAR-F Drill 01: gaps from 2026-11-18
notes: Fresh scenarios on the sub-skills missed on 2026-11-18, weighted to repeat misses (1.4, 3.3, 2.4, 1.7, 4.1, 5.6). Single-answer, like the real CCAR-F.

questions.scenario: A support agent has a process_refund tool. Policy: refunds over $500 must have a manager approval id. Production logs show the agent occasionally skips this despite a clear system prompt.
questions.stem: Which change makes the guarantee hold?

options.text: Add "NEVER refund over $500 without approval" in bold to the system prompt and CLAUDE.md.
options.rationale: Emphasis is still a request. The model usually complies, but "usually" is not a guarantee.

options.text: Add three few-shot examples of the agent declining large refunds.
options.rationale: Examples shift probabilities; they do not make a path impossible.

options.text: Add a PreToolUse hook on the refund tool that reads tool_input.amount and denies calls over $500 without an approval id.
options.rationale: A hook runs in code before the tool executes, reads the real arguments, and can deny. That is enforcement.

options.text: Ask the model to double-check its refund amount before calling the tool.
options.rationale: A self-check by the same model is another instruction, not a gate.

questions.scenario: Same refund agent. You are writing the PreToolUse hook configuration.
questions.stem: Where should the hook matcher and the amount check each live?

options.text: Matcher: "process_refund"; amount check inside the hook callback reading tool_input.
options.rationale: The matcher selects by tool name; arguments are only visible to the callback.

options.text: Matcher: "amount > 500"; callback just returns allow.
options.rationale: Matchers match tool names, not argument values.

options.text: Matcher: "refund"; amount check in CLAUDE.md.
options.rationale: CLAUDE.md is context, not enforcement.

options.text: No matcher; check the amount in the next user turn.
options.rationale: Too late; the tool already ran.

questions.scenario: A billing agent must verify the customer before issuing credit. Sometimes it calls issue_credit using an id taken from the user message.
questions.stem: What must a gate on issue_credit enforce?

options.text: A larger max_tokens so the model has room to follow the sequence.
options.rationale: Unrelated to ordering.

options.text: A prompt line telling the model to call lookup_order first.
options.rationale: Ordering by instruction is not a guarantee.

options.text: A retry loop that re-asks the model when it skips lookup_order.
options.rationale: The credit has already been issued by then.

options.text: That lookup_order has returned a verified customer id for this conversation before issue_credit is allowed, failing closed if not.
options.rationale: Gate the dependent tool on a recorded prerequisite and deny by default.

questions.scenario: The agent decides it cannot resolve a chargeback dispute and hands off to a human queue.
questions.stem: What should the escalation handoff to the human queue contain?

options.text: The full 80-turn transcript so nothing is lost.
options.rationale: Pushes the work onto the human; no actionable summary.

options.text: The ticket id, the finding so far, and the concrete action the human should take.
options.rationale: A handoff is id + finding + concrete action, so the human does not restart.

options.text: Only "customer is upset, please help".
options.rationale: No state, no action.

options.text: A link to the agent's system prompt.
options.rationale: Not task state.

questions.scenario: Test files sit next to the code they test (src/billing/invoice.ts and src/billing/invoice.test.ts). You want testing conventions loaded only when Claude works with test files.
questions.stem: Which rule file glob matches the stated intent?

options.text: paths: ["**/tests/**"]
options.rationale: Matches a tests/ directory, not co-located *.test.ts files next to the source.

options.text: paths: ["**/*.test.ts", "**/*.test.tsx"]
options.rationale: Matches test files wherever they live, including next to the code.

options.text: paths: ["src/**"]
options.rationale: Matches all source, including non-test files.

options.text: No paths field; mention tests in the rule text.
options.rationale: Without paths the rule loads every session, which defeats the point.

questions.scenario: A 4,000-token style guide is referenced from CLAUDE.md via @docs/style.md. The team assumes it only loads when relevant.
questions.stem: What does importing the style guide with an @ line in CLAUDE.md do to context usage?

options.text: It loads the file only when Claude first needs it.
options.rationale: @imports are not lazy.

options.text: It loads it only for subagents.
options.rationale: No such scoping.

options.text: It is ignored unless a paths field is present.
options.rationale: paths belongs to .claude/rules, not @imports.

options.text: It loads the file at launch together with CLAUDE.md, so it costs context in every session.
options.rationale: Imports expand at launch; the cost is paid up front.

questions.scenario: A team wants notes for human editors inside the shared CLAUDE.md that Claude should not read.
questions.stem: Which mechanism keeps maintainer notes out of Claude's context while still in the committed CLAUDE.md?

options.text: Wrap them in block-level HTML comments.
options.rationale: Block-level HTML comments are stripped before injection.

options.text: Place them under a final "## Maintainer notes" heading, which is skipped.
options.rationale: No section is skipped by position.

options.text: Put them in CLAUDE.local.md.
options.rationale: Personal and gitignored, so other editors never see them.

options.text: Prefix each line with "IGNORE:".
options.rationale: Just text, still injected.

questions.scenario: Everyone on the team needs the same ERP MCP server defined in the repo, but the API token must never be committed.
questions.stem: Which setup satisfies both the sharing and the secrecy requirement?

options.text: User scope with the token written into the config.
options.rationale: Nothing reaches the repo, so the team gets no checked-in config.

options.text: Project scope with the real token, repo set to private.
options.rationale: A secret in git remains a secret in git.

options.text: Project scope .mcp.json with "Authorization": "Bearer ${ERP_TOKEN}"; each person exports ERP_TOKEN.
options.rationale: Shared via git; only the variable name is committed.

options.text: Project scope .mcp.json added to .gitignore.
options.rationale: Defeats sharing.

questions.scenario: A code-audit run ended with error_max_turns after reading 60 files. You want to keep the analysis done so far and just keep going.

options.text: Fork the session and give the fork a higher max_turns.
options.rationale: Fork creates a new session for diverging, not continuing.

options.text: Re-run the original prompt as a new query with a higher max_turns.
options.rationale: Empty context; the reads and analysis are repeated.

options.text: Start a new session and paste a summary.
options.rationale: Loses the working context and invites drift.

options.text: Resume by session_id with a higher max_turns.
options.rationale: Same session, full context kept, limit raised.

questions.scenario: A review prompt says "flag misleading comments only if you are very sure." Reviewers complain of noise and misses.
questions.stem: Which replacement is an explicit criterion?

options.text: Report only comments you are highly confident are wrong.
options.rationale: A confidence filter.

options.text: Report a comment only when it states a behavior the code contradicts, citing the line.
options.rationale: Two reviewers applying it get the same result.

options.text: Report comments a senior engineer would agree are misleading.
options.rationale: Subjective.

options.text: Report comments with at least 80% estimated accuracy.
options.rationale: A threshold on self-assessment.

questions.scenario: An extraction prompt keeps inventing precise quantities when the source text is vague. Rewording the instruction twice did not help.

options.text: Make quantity nullable, with few-shot examples that map "a couple tablets" to a value and one where quantity is absent returning null.
options.rationale: Gives a legitimate "not stated" and shows both cases.

options.text: Require quantity in grams and reject non-numeric values.
options.rationale: Demands precision, creating fabrication.

options.text: Add a synonym list for quantity phrases.
options.rationale: Same lever as the instruction that already failed.

options.text: Lower temperature to 0.
options.rationale: Does not remove the incentive to fabricate.

questions.scenario: Extraction passes strict schema validation, but line items sum to $940 while order_total says $980.

options.text: A tighter JSON schema with min/max on each field.
options.rationale: Cannot express a relation between fields.

options.text: Retry at temperature 0 until the schema passes.
options.rationale: The schema is blind to this.

options.text: A code check that recomputes the sum and compares to order_total, retrying or routing to review on mismatch.
options.rationale: Validates meaning in code.

options.text: Ask the model to be careful with totals.
options.rationale: An instruction, not a check.

questions.scenario: Several research subagents feed a compression step before a synthesis agent. Reports read well, but nobody can tell which document supports which claim.

options.text: A summary paragraph per topic plus a numbered URL list at the end.
options.rationale: A bibliography, not a claim-to-source mapping.

options.text: One record per claim: short claim text plus source URL, document name and excerpt in labelled fields on the same record.
options.rationale: The link survives any further compression.

options.text: Label each group with the subagent that found it.
options.rationale: Says who found it, not what supports it.

options.text: Drop low-confidence claims and describe evidence in prose.
options.rationale: Loses claims and the mapping.

questions.scenario: The coordinator prompt says "Use the data-analyst agent to summarise Q3 churn." The data-analyst AgentDefinition has a vague description.

options.text: Nothing; naming is a request, and the description should say when the subagent applies.
options.rationale: Claude still decides; the description remains the signal.

options.text: Delegation always happens, whatever the description says.
options.rationale: Stronger than any doc states.

options.text: Delegation, but only for subagents loaded from filesystem files.
options.rationale: Invented restriction.

options.text: Delegation once the name is matched against the description text.
options.rationale: Names are not matched that way.

questions.scenario: A subagent audits every use of a deprecated API across a monorepo, producing thousands of lines. The coordinator's context must stay small but it may need to inspect one chain later.
questions.stem: Which instruction to the subagent best fits?

options.text: Return the full transcript of every search.
options.rationale: Fills the coordinator's context.

options.text: Return only "done".
options.rationale: Loses the drill-down requirement.

options.text: Return a prose overview with no file paths.
options.rationale: Nothing to drill into.

options.text: Write the detail to a findings file; return a short summary plus the file path.
options.rationale: Small context now, detail recoverable later.

questions.scenario: Date extraction is 93% accurate overall but only 68% on handwritten forms; typed forms are 97%.

options.text: Random review sized to the 93% overall accuracy.
options.rationale: Treats the weak segment like the rest.

options.text: Manual entry for every date, retire the model for this field.
options.rationale: Throws away the 97% segment.

options.text: Route handwritten-form dates to a human; let typed-form dates through unreviewed.
options.rationale: Review follows the weak segment.

options.text: Prompt the model to assume DD/MM and release unreviewed.
options.rationale: A guess released without review.

questions.scenario: A customer says twice, "I want to speak to a person about my invoice." The agent's first reply tried to fix the invoice.
questions.stem: What should the agent do next?

options.text: Offer a discount, then escalate if declined.
options.rationale: Ignores the explicit request.

options.text: Ask what the issue is, then decide whether to escalate.
options.rationale: Interrogates instead of routing.

options.text: Transfer to a human now, passing the account and the issue so far.
options.rationale: An explicit request is honored immediately, with context.

options.text: Resolve the issue itself and mention a human is available.
options.rationale: Overrides what the customer said.

questions.scenario: A fixed four-step chain for onboarding a new data source works until some sources need an unplanned authentication-mapping step discovered only while reading their docs.

options.text: The chain lacks a final validation step.
options.rationale: A fixed chain cannot absorb discovered steps; adding one stage does not change that.

options.text: The required steps depend on what the input contains, so the team needs adaptive decomposition.
options.rationale: Unpredictable subtasks mean orchestrator-style planning.

options.text: The model is too small to hold the chain.
options.rationale: Unrelated.

options.text: Add a seventh fixed step for the new case.
options.rationale: The next input will need an eighth.
